chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Mūsā ibn Saʿdān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from al-Muthannā, from al-Ḥasan al-Ṣayqal, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man performed tayammum, then stood and prayed, and a river passed by him after he had prayed one rakʿah. He said: Then let him perform ghusl and begin the salat anew.
So I said to him: He had already completed all of his salat. He said: He does not repeat it.

So this report may be understood as meaning that he had entered into the salat before the end of the time, and thus it became obligatory for him to recommence, according to what we have said. It is also possible that it is to be understood as referring to a kind of recommendation.

key_terms.الْوَقْتِ: the prescribed time of the prayer
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum as a substitute purification in the absence of water
key_terms.لَا يُعِيدُهَا: he does not repeat the prayer
key_terms.نَهْرٌ: a river, indicating the availability of water
key_terms.يَسْتَقْبِلِ الصَّلَاةَ: begin the salat anew from the start

ai.seo_question: If someone starts praying with tayammum and then finds water during the salat, must the prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of one who begins salat with tayammum and then finds water during the prayer. It distinguishes between finding water before completion of the prayer and after completing it, while the compiler notes possible ways to reconcile the report in legal interpretation.
